Debt crisis in EU faces the tight bank loans and global financial market is in volatility due to the pessimistic attitude** EU crisis is now viewed as a heavy hit to global economy and financial market. However, efforts to solve the crisis are just in discussion level, and real conclusions and actions haven’t yet broadly approved by market, therefore the national debt in a single nation and the pessimistic attitude towards economy have gradually moved to Italy and France and other developed nations. By September 20, S & P lowered the sovereign debt credit rating of Italy from A+ to A, with a negative vision. Italy is the third largest economy following Germany and France and the largest state treasury bonds issuer in EU, accounting for 25% in EU, higher than the 24% of Germany and 20% of France. A lower credit rating of Italy will affect global bond market and make it harder to rescue EU nations. Before any decisive action is taken to deal with the EU debt crisis, the impact of intermittent will become more frequent, especially when the market is in a process to continuously re-definite risk asset, and it is hard to avoid the re-configure of global asset, which will hit the financial institutions in EU again, whose liquidity and bank capital have already faced severe test by the huge outflow of funds. For example, outflow of funds in Italian banking industry has exceeded 100 bln dollars in recent one year, and deposits in Germany have declined by as much as 12%, not to mention the worse Greece and Ireland. Before the peak period of national debt due in 2012, debt crisis will continue to hit financial market and real economy. EU debt crisis worsened the situation of banks with high national bonds, if these bonds are likely to default, then banks have to lower the value of their held national bonds and the asset of banks and their financing capability. And the credit crun

ch will result in the tight liquidity among banks. Banks in Italy and Greece hold the highest proportion of national bonds. And the sovereign debt crisis reduces the value of bank collateral assets and is bad to the bank financing. And a lower credit rating will make it hard for banks to get funds in public market, which can be seen from the new high of interest spread of 3-month Libor and OIS since March of 2009. The problems in banks will reduce their support to real economies and further deter the recovery of weak economies, which can be seen in the following aspects: firstly debt crisis will lead to high yield of national bonds and financing cost, while the set of enterprise bond and CDS price is usually based on yield of risk-free national bonds, therefore it will raise the financing cost of enterprise in bond market, and credit crisis will spread to market and the overall macro economy. Credit rating of enterprises doing main business in the nation will also be dragged down, raising its financing cost. Besides, a deteriorated government fiscal will increase its financing demand and the government will increase its expenditure, which will reduce private consumption and investment, and largely restrain private investment and economic growth. 3 300,000

China might loosen its tight economic policies when facing uncertainties in overseas market** Just like what we have pointed out in our last 2 reports, the tight economic policies, eyeing the inflation might bring some bad effect to China’s real economy. There were rumors saying the private high interest loans and the flee of business owners and close of their enterprises due to the breaking of the funding chain in private enterprises. Although enterprises couldn’t get loans from banks, they can use the form of trade financing. Under the current tight financial situation, the acceptance of enterprises couldn’t be discounted, therefore the former fund and operating mode are broken down, and the declining non ferrous metals prices deteriorates financing, so we believe it will spread to the copper and aluminum industry. Inflation has become the focus in macro economy since H2 2010. Output gap has continued to decline for 18 months since Feb 2010, but began to fluctuate in recent 8 months and dropped again in recent 2 months. From the prospect of the lagged effects of conduction (output gap is usually 7 months ahead of CPI), inflation reached its peak in Q3 and would decline gradually after Q4. We noticed their relationship mode changed-the indicating function of output gap weakened, indicating that the driven force of CPI and competition was different during this period, and we judged this round of inflation wasn’t driven by demand, but if the inflation was triggered by excessive currency, while the 7 economic growth wasn’t stimulated by this reason, then it would contradict our common sense. We can ask what is the inner engine of China’s economic growth? We should re-think this. 15

Chart 9 China’s liquidity is back to the normal level 8 ## **3. Overview of China’s non ferrous metals industry** ###

**3.1 Slow growth rate of metal output and changing development mode** 

Output of 10 non ferrous metals in China reached 22.53 Mt in Jan-Aug 2011, up by 8.2% year on year, 5.5% lower than the average growth rate during 2006-2010. It is estimated total output will reach 35.80 Mt throughout 2011, up by around 10% year on year, among which refined copper is 5.15 Mt, up by 12% year on year and aluminum is 18 Mt, up by 9.8% year on year. 

But the raw material output rose substantially on contrary. Metal output of copper concentrate reached 810,000t in Jan-Aug and is estimated to reach 1.20 Mt in 2011, up by over 10% year on year; alumina output was 23.30 Mt during Jan-Aug and is estimated to reach 36.75 Mt in 2011, up by 26.9% year on year. 

### **3.2 Enterprises with energy and resources have more economic benefit** 

Above scale non ferrous metals companies achieved 99.55 bln yuan of profit in Jan-Jul 2011, up by 62.93% year on year, ranking the forefront among domestic industries. It is estimated that total profit will be 280 bln yuan in 2011, the historical level. 

Enterprises with energy and resources have more economic benefit. For example Jiangxi Copper with rich resources achieved 5.063 bln yuan of profit in H1 2011, higher than other domestic copper companies. 

### **3.3 FAI moves towards west** 

FAI in non ferrous metals industry reached 287.1 bln yuan in Jan-Aug 2011, up by 30.1% year on year, among which west 12 provinces completed 97.42 bln yuan, up by 37.5% year on year, 7.4% higher than the average national level. 

### **3.4 Export value of precious metals and rare earth rises substantially** 

Export value of precious metals and rare earth rises substantially in the first 8 months of 2011, among which Antimony was $400 mln, up by 55.9%, Tungsten was $ 780 mln, up by 80.4% year on year and rare earth was $ 1.92 bln, up by 202.1% year on year. 

### **3.5 Prices of main non ferrous metals continue to fluctuate at a high level** 

Copper price stabilized at $9,000 per tonne in the first 8 months, up by 30.3% year on year, and it is estimated average price will be $9,215 per tonne in 2011; aluminum price averaged at $2,526 per tonne, up by 19.1% year on year and is predicted to be $2,553 per tonne in 2011 in international market. 

While price at domestic market was weaker than that in international market in 2011. Refined copper price averaged at 70,160 yuan/t in Jan-Aug, up by 24.4% year on year,

and is estimated to reach 71,196 yuan/t in 2011; aluminum price was 16,955 yuan/t, up by 8.2% year on year, and is estimated to reach 17100 yuan/t throughout 2011. 

### **3.6 Industrial adjustment and technological upgrading** 

Guided by the national polices, some advanced technologies like “A new cathode structure of aluminum energy-saving technology”, “Copper-oxygen bottom-blowing energy saving technology” are adopted and used by enterprises, making the technological equipments in non ferrous metals industry reach world-leading

level. In H1 of 2011, integrated AC power consumption of domestic aluminum ingot reached 13.948 kwh/t, down by 60 kwh/t compared with the same period in 2010, saving 520 mln kwh power. Comprehensive energy consumption of copper smelting was 362.3 kg standard coal/t, down by 1.5% compared with the same period in 2010, reaching world leading level. And the secondary non ferrous metals industry, with relatively outdated equipments also actively phased out its backward capacity and updated technologies, therefore its demand for advanced technology rose rapidly. 

Strength of key enterprises intensified substantially with a continuous promotion of strategic consolidation. It is estimated that non ferrous metals company with main operating income of over 100 bln yuan would increase from 1 in 2008 to 5 in 2011, and the proportion of the top 5 copper and aluminum smelting enterprises reached 70% and 50%. 

The development of non ferrous metals and new materials industries was attached great importance. Some importance products, like aluminum strip and copper ended their dependence on import, and some enterprises have the capability to compete with some international companies. 

## **4. Analysis of non ferrous metals industry in 2012** 

Economic environment in China and abroad was still complex and faced a lot of uncertainties. Judged by the demand and supply relationship, demand of global non ferrous metals will continue to increase in 2012, and copper and aluminum and other main metals will have a stable production underpinned by growing demand. 

### **4.1 Analysis on world non ferrous metals market** 

It is estimated that global demand of refined copper will reach 19.85 Mt, up by 3.71% year on year, and output will be 19.63 Mt, up by 3.69% year on year, with demand slightly higher than output. Aluminum demand is estimated to be 46.73 Mt, up by 2.16% year on year, and output to be 47.31 Mt, up by 3.2% year on year, with around 580,000t of oversupply. 

And price of main metals will be closely linked with financial environment in 2012. The interest rate of USD is the major factor in deciding metal price. If dollar index rises, then metal price drops, and vice versa. It is estimated that refined copper price will be 

10 

averaging at $8,000-9,000 per tonne, and aluminum price at $2,000-2,500 per tonne. 

### **4.2 Analysis of domestic non ferrous metals market** 

China’s macro economic policy will continue to be stabilizing in 2012, and a stable price will be the top priority in macro regulation. Further measures will be given to maintain a stable and rapid economic development, regulate economic structure and manage inflation, accelerate the transformation of development pattern so as to achieve a balanced and rapid economic development. 

It is now the key period in building a well-off society. Domestic demand for non ferrous metals continues to increase with the development of industrialization, urbanization and informatization, and the develop

ment of transportation, energy, affordable houses, infrastructure, and the build of a new countryside. The development of new strategic industries also provide strong support to non ferrous metal industry, besides, new environmental standards also require the industry to update its development mode so as to achieve new and higher goals. 

It is estimated domestic demand for refined copper will be 7.85 Mt in 2012, up by 6.37% year on year, 2.66% higher than the global level; aluminum demand will be 20.10 Mt, up by 8.45% year on year, 6.3% higher than global level. 

Production of non ferrous metals will continue to increase in 2012 due to the robust demand. It is predicted that refined copper will reach 5.65 Mt, up by 9.6% year on year, with 2.20 Mt of gap between demand; aluminum output will be 19.80 Mt, up by 10% year on year, which can satisfy domestic demand. 

And domestic price might be weaker than international market in 2012 due to the policies to curb inflation. Refined copper price might average at 69,000 yuan/t, and aluminum at 16,800 yuan/t.
